disposition_reason: Nine metals were measured by ICP-MS in 160 field potatoes from Moquegua, a copper-mining department; Tables 2 to 4 give means by altitude, cultivar type and zone, and the text gives the overall ranges.

study.design: Field survey of 160 potato samples with paired soils across four agroecological altitude regions and nine agricultural zones
study.origin: farm fields, Moquegua department, Peru, 58-3934 m a.s.l. (copper-mining region)
study.method: Edible portion incl. skin and pulp; ICP-MS (EPA 200.3/EPA 6010B); 14 preliminary samples for As, Cd, Pb by NOM-117-SSA1-1994; soils by ICP-OES
study.lod_text: LOD/LOQ in Table S2 (supplement, not available)
study.qa: INACAL-accredited laboratory (NTP-ISO/IEC 17025); no CRM or recovery reported in main text

controls.outcome: modern higher in As (0.050 vs 0.014), Cr (0.032 vs 0.011), Al (7.261 vs 4.012 mg/kg); native higher in Cd (0.010 vs 0.007) and Mn; Pb not different (0.036 vs 0.049 mg/kg)

controls.comparator: Chala & Yunga vs Quechua vs Suni
controls.outcome: As 0.065 -> 0.037 -> 0.012 mg/kg and Cr 0.067 -> 0.015 -> 0.010 mg/kg falling with altitude; Pb and Cu not different

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FAO/WHO and EU maximum levels for Cd and Pb in potatoes

unresolved: Tables S1-S4 (supplement: zone membership, LODs, descriptive statistics) were not found next to the PDF.
Discussion lists Suni Pb 0.049 and Cu 1.469 mg/kg, which match the native-cultivar row of Table 2 rather than the Suni row (0.038 and 1.408).
